idiom_name: regular class with an immutable val id; never a data class
implementation_notes: Kotlin's default equals for a regular class is identity equality inherited from Any - exactly the entity semantics - so the language idiom is largely negative: do not use a data class, whose compiler-generated equals/hashCode compares every primary-constructor property and whose copy() fabricates detached duplicates of a managed entity. Model the entity as a regular (usually open) class with an immutable val id and mutable var attributes whose changes go through methods; for JPA the entity classes must be open for proxy creation and provide a no-arg constructor, and equals should compare the id only with a class-based hashCode so the hash cannot change when the id is assigned. Data classes remain the natural choice for value objects and DTOs.
pitfalls: data class generates equals/hashCode over all properties, so a managed entity disappears from a Set after a field changes; keep data classes for DTOs and value objects.
Kotlin classes are final by default, so Hibernate cannot build proxies; mark entities open (or apply the allopen/jpa compiler plugin) and give them a no-arg constructor.
Deriving hashCode from an auto-generated id changes after persistence; use a constant class hash or an id assigned in the constructor so sets and maps stay valid.
